english.title: Incur general election expenses in excess of pre-candidacy maximum
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were guilty of an illegal practice in that you were

(A)_[a candidate]_
(B)_[an election agent]_

who

(C)_[incurred]_
(D)_[authorised the incurring of]_

election expenses of **(..SPECIFY AMOUNT..) for

(E)_[yourself]_
(F)_[a candidate, namely **(..SPECIFY CANDIDATE..),]_

in respect of a matter which was used, where Parliament was not dissolved until after the period of 55 months beginning with the day on which that Parliament first met, during the period beginning immediately after the 55-month period and ending with the day on which

(G)_[you]_
(H)_[the person]_

became a candidate at the parliamentary general election which followed the dissolution, and which were in excess of the maximum amount permitted, namely **(..SPECIFY PERMITTED AMOUNT..), when you knew or ought reasonably to have known that the expenses would be incurred in excess of that maximum amount
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 76ZA(5) and 169 of the Representation of the People Act 1983.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
candidate or election agent incurred or authorised the incurring of
election expenses as mentioned in section 76ZA(1) in excess of the permitted amount
when you knew or ought reasonably to have known that the expenses would be incurred in excess of that amount

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex see section 176Note
On the 12th March 2015, the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' Court was removed - as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
